answer: A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 162 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The beacon detector writes to ledge, and thread publishes every merge. Submissions that land within 193 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
